u1s0: Grounds for divorce are regulations specifying the circumstances under which a person will be granted a divorce.
u2s0: Adultery is the most common grounds for divorce.
u3s0: However, there are countries that view male adultery differently than female adultery as grounds for divorce.
u4s0: Cruel and inhuman treatment constitute as grounds for divorce.
u5s0: In a proper defense, acceptable differences enable the defendant to have the ability to arrange grounds for divorce.
u6s0: Some examples for grounds for divorce are: Adultery Alcoholism Disability Abandonment (legal) Imprisonment Domestic violence (Including physical, sexual, or mental abuse of the other spouse and/or the child/children of the couple.)
u7s0: Different states accept different grounds for divorce.
u8s0: For example, some states only accept no-fault divorce where other states accept both fault and no-fault grounds for divorce.
u9s0: == United States == In the United States, each state has distinctive reference names for grounds for divorce.
u10s0: A no fault divorce can be granted on grounds such as irretrievable breakdown of the marriage, irreconcilable differences, incompatibility, or after a period of separation, depending on the state.
u11s0: Grounds for at fault divorce include adultery, cruelty, abandonment, and criminal conviction.
u12s0: == Worldwide view == Many countries around the world, including the United States, require grounds for divorce.
u13s0: In some Native American societies, adultery is grounds, but other considerations are factored into the divorce equation.
u14s0: A frequent issue in family law relates to what situations create grounds for divorce.
u15s0: Chinese ancient law consisted of three types of divorce that were recognized: 1) Mutual consent; 2) repudiation of "seven grounds for men and three grounds for women"; 3) "intolerable acts against principles of conjugality."
